 [Tomorrow's Weather] Cloudy and Rainy Nationwide Monday... Early-Winter Chill to Continue for Now
 by Cho Seongpill 
 Published 08 Nov.2026 20:02(KST) 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Monday, the 9th, will be mostly cloudy and chilly across the country.
 A pedestrian wearing a heavy coat crosses the street at Sejong-daero Intersection in Seoul. Yonhap News Agency
 View original image 
 According to the Korea Meteorological Administration on the 8th, morning lows the following day are forecast to range from 2 to 11°C, and daytime highs from 11 to 15°C, similar to or slightly below the seasonal averages of 2 to 11°C in the morning and 13 to 19°C during the day. Chilly weather is expected to continue for the time being. Morning temperatures are expected to fall below freezing in some areas, particularly inland and mountainous parts of Gangwon on the 9th and inland areas of the central region and eastern Jeonbuk on the 10th. The temperature range between day and night will widen to 10 to 15°C in most areas, so people should take care of their health.
 In the Seoul metropolitan area, a few raindrops of less than 0.1 mm may fall before dawn. Rain will begin in Jeju Island and Jeonnam in the morning, and in Jeonbuk, Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and other areas from the afternoon, letting up only in the late afternoon. Rain is also expected along the east coast and in the mountains of Gangwon, as well as along the east coast of Gyeongbuk. Expected precipitation is 5 to 30 mm in Jeju Island; 5 to 10 mm along the east coast and in the mountains of Gangwon, in Gwangju and Jeonnam, and in Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam; and less than 5 mm in Jeonbuk, inland areas of Daegu and Gyeongbuk, and the northeastern mountains of Gyeongbuk.

 Waves are expected to reach 0.5 to 3.5 m in the waters off the east coast, 0.5 to 2.5 m in the waters off the west coast, and 0.5 to 3.0 m in the waters off the south coast. Wave heights in the outer waters within about 200 km of the coastline are forecast to reach 1.0 to 4.0 m in the East and South Seas and 1.0 to 3.5 m in the West Sea.
